# Leaky tap washer

## Symptom

Bath cold tap dripping, about one drop every 2 seconds. Measured it: 280ml in an hour into a jug. Lucía said it kept her up, so it got done on a Saturday.

## Kit

- 1/2" tap washers, 12.5mm rubber, mixed bag of 10 from Screwfix, item 18452, £3.49
- O-rings, the assorted box I already had
- 22mm spanner + an adjustable for holding the tap body so I don't twist the pipe
- WD-40 Silicone, not normal WD-40, for the spindle threads
- Old towel in the bath so nothing goes down the plughole

## How it went

1. Isolation: there's no isolation valve on the bath feeds (of course), so it was the main stop tap under the stairs. Opened the kitchen cold to drain down
2. Prised the chrome cap off the cross head, flat screwdriver, it's a push-fit cover over a 6mm grub screw
3. Shroud unscrewed by hand after a bit of persuasion
4. Headgear nut 22mm. Held the tap body with the adjustable. Came off fine
5. Old washer was split right across and hard as a biscuit, held on by a little nut on the jumper. Swapped it
6. Cleaned the seat with a scouring pad. Seat looked OK, no pitting, so no need for a reseating tool
7. Put it back, turned the water on slowly, no drip

Total about 50 minutes, most of it finding the stop tap key.

## Lessons

- Taps are Pegler Bath Pillars from the 90s, not ceramic disc. Ceramic disc taps don't have a washer at all, you swap the cartridge
- Fit isolation valves on the bath feeds next time the bath panel is off. Wrote it on the list
- If the drip comes back within months, the seat is worn, not the washer
